content.text:
I built Circuit Bench, a desktop circuit simulator with the same core workflow as the original, and it passes Craft Anything's build and screenshot checks. You pick parts from a parts bin (resistors, capacitors, inductors, potentiometer, switch, sources, diodes, Zener, LED, lamp, voltmeter, ammeter, voltage probe) and place them on a dotted sheet. You wire them by clicking pins, then press the green Run button to watch it live. A multimeter, a function generator and a two-channel oscilloscope (with trigger and measuring cursors) update as it runs. LEDs and lamps glow, and you toggle switches with a key or a click.

It also runs the classic analyses: DC operating point, AC frequency sweep, transient and DC sweep. Results show in a graph window you can export to CSV. You also get undo/redo, copy/paste, save and open, an electrical rules check, a SPICE netlist export and seven ready-made example circuits. The app opens running an RC filter with the oscilloscope showing both waves. I checked the math on every example (for instance the voltage divider reads 3.84 V and the Zener holds 5.17 V).

As you chose, this version leaves out transistors, op-amps, logic gates, microcontrollers and board layout. The look is my own design, since there was no copy of the original to compare against. The name and visuals are original too, with no branding from the real product.

A good next step would be a Bode plotter instrument (a live frequency-response display, like the original has), or adding transistors and op-amps so you can build amplifiers.

@echo off
rem Builds Circuit Bench for Windows and puts CircuitBench.exe in the "dist" folder.
rem Needs Rust: install it once from https://rustup.rs (choose the default options).
where cargo >nul 2>nul

  echo Rust is not installed. Get it from https://rustup.rs and run this script again.
  pause
  exit /b 1
)

cargo build --release

  echo The build failed - see the messages above.
  pause
  exit /b 1
)
if not exist dist mkdir dist
copy /y target\release\circuit_bench.exe dist\CircuitBench.exe >nul
echo Done! Double-click dist\CircuitBench.exe to start Circuit Bench.
pause

# Circuit Bench

A circuit design and simulation bench: draw schematics or build on a 2D breadboard,
then run them live with meters, an oscilloscope, a Bode plotter and more.

## Windows

1. Install Rust once from https://rustup.rs (default options; when it offers the
   Microsoft C++ build tools, accept them).
2. Double-click `build-windows.bat` in this folder.
3. Start `dist\CircuitBench.exe`.

Settings (theme, grid, animations) are kept in `%USERPROFILE%\.circuit_bench_settings.json`.
Circuits are saved as `.cbs` files, by default in your Documents folder.

## macOS and Linux

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/circuit_bench
```

Linux also needs the usual desktop graphics libraries (X11/Wayland, OpenGL) that most desktops already have.

## Options

- `--example <n>` open a built-in example (0–8)
- `--view breadboard` start on the breadboard
- `--theme <Light|Dark|Midnight|Blueprint|Sepia|Forest>`
- `--screenshot <file.png>` draw a few frames, save a picture and quit

   Microsoft C++ build tools, accept them).
2. Double-click `build-windows.bat` in this folder.
3. Start `dist\CircuitBench.exe`.

Settings (theme, grid, animations) are kept in `%USERPROFILE%\.circuit_bench_settings.json`.
Circuits are saved as `.cbs` files, by default in your Documents folder.

## macOS and Linux

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/circuit_bench
```

Linux also needs the usual desktop graphics libraries (X11/Wayland, OpenGL) that most desktops already have.

## Options

- `--example <n>` open a built-in example (0–8)
- `--view breadboard` start on the breadboard
- `--theme <Light|Dark|Midnight|Blueprint|Sepia|Forest>`
- `--screenshot <file.png>` draw a few frames, save a picture and quit

# Builds Circuit Bench for Windows, macOS and Linux on every push.
# Pushing a tag such as v1.0.0 also publishes a GitHub Release with the downloads attached.
name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            artifact: CircuitBench-windows
            binary: target/release/circuit_bench.exe
            packaged: CircuitBench.exe
          - os: macos-latest
            artifact: CircuitBench-macos
            binary: target/release/circuit_bench
            packaged: CircuitBench
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            artifact: CircuitBench-linux
            binary: target/release/circuit_bench
            packaged: CircuitBench
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Linux desktop libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libxkbcommon-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libx11-dev libxcursor-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libwayland-dev

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --release

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --release

      - name: Package
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp "${{ matrix.binary }}" "dist/${{ matrix.packaged }}"
          cp README.md LICENSE dist/
          cd dist
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then
            7z a "../${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip" .
          else
            chmod +x "${{ matrix.packaged }}"
            zip -r "../${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip" .
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
          path: ${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip

      - name: Attach to release
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: ${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip

# Circuit Bench

A circuit design and simulation bench: draw schematics or build on a 2D breadboard,
then run them live with meters, an oscilloscope, a Bode plotter and more.

![Breadboard view](docs/breadboard.png)

| Schematic with a live oscilloscope (Dark theme) | Op-amp amplifier (Blueprint theme) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Schematic](docs/schematic-dark.png) | ![Op-amp](docs/opamp-blueprint.png) |

## Features

- **Schematic editor**: parts bin, grid, wiring by clicking pins, move/rotate/copy/undo, properties for every part.
- **2D breadboard**: power rails and connected strips, realistic parts, coloured jumper wires; hover a hole to see what it is joined to.
- **Live simulation**: LEDs glow, lamps light, motors spin, buzzers sound off visually, fuses blow, current flows along wires.
- **Instruments**: multimeter, function generator, 2-channel oscilloscope, wattmeter, Bode plotter, frequency counter.
- **Analyses**: DC operating point, AC sweep, transient and DC sweep, shown in a grapher with CSV export.
- **Parts**: resistors, capacitors, inductors, potentiometer, fuse, DC/AC/clock sources, diodes, Zener, LEDs, op-amp,
  switches and push buttons, lamp, motor, buzzer, voltmeter, ammeter, probe.
- **Themes**: Light, Dark, Midnight, Blueprint, Sepia and Forest.
- Save/open circuits, SPICE netlist export, nine example circuits.

## Download

Ready-made builds for Windows, macOS and Linux are on the **Releases** page of this repository.

## Build it yourself

### Windows

1. Install Rust once from https://rustup.rs (default options; when it offers the
   Microsoft C++ build tools, accept them).
2. Double-click `build-windows.bat` in this folder.
3. Start `dist\CircuitBench.exe`.

Settings (theme, grid, animations) are kept in `%USERPROFILE%\.circuit_bench_settings.json`.
Circuits are saved as `.cbs` files, by default in your Documents folder.

### macOS and Linux

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/circuit_bench
```

Linux also needs the usual desktop graphics libraries (X11/Wayland, OpenGL) that most desktops already have.

## Options

- `--example <n>` open a built-in example (0–8)
- `--view breadboard` start on the breadboard
- `--theme <Light|Dark|Midnight|Blueprint|Sepia|Forest>`
- `--screenshot <file.png>` draw a few frames, save a picture and quit

## Publishing a release

Every push builds the app for all three systems automatically (see the **Actions** tab).
To publish downloads, create a tag that starts with `v` (for example `v1.0.0`) — on GitHub:
**Releases → Draft a new release → Choose a tag → type `v1.0.0` → Publish**. The builds are attached to it a few minutes later.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

- **Schematic editor**: parts bin, grid, wiring by clicking pins, move/rotate/copy/undo, properties for every part.
- **2D breadboard**: power rails and connected strips, realistic parts, coloured jumper wires; hover a hole to see what it is joined to.
- **Live simulation**: LEDs glow, lamps light, motors spin, buzzers sound off visually, fuses blow, current flows along wires.
- **Instruments**: multimeter, function generator, 2-channel oscilloscope, wattmeter, Bode plotter, frequency counter.
- **Analyses**: DC operating point, AC sweep, transient and DC sweep, shown in a grapher with CSV export.
- **Parts**: resistors, capacitors, inductors, potentiometer, fuse, DC/AC/clock sources, diodes, Zener, LEDs, op-amp,
  switches and push buttons, lamp, motor, buzzer, voltmeter, ammeter, probe.
- **Themes**: Light, Dark, Midnight, Blueprint, Sepia and Forest.
- Save/open circuits, SPICE netlist export, nine example circuits.

## Download

Ready-made builds for Windows, macOS and Linux are on the **Releases** page of this repository.

## Build it yourself

### Windows

1. Install Rust once from https://rustup.rs (default options; when it offers the
   Microsoft C++ build tools, accept them).
2. Double-click `build-windows.bat` in this folder.
3. Start `dist\CircuitBench.exe`.

Settings (theme, grid, animations) are kept in `%USERPROFILE%\.circuit_bench_settings.json`.
Circuits are saved as `.cbs` files, by default in your Documents folder.

### macOS and Linux

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/circuit_bench
```

Linux also needs the usual desktop graphics libraries (X11/Wayland, OpenGL) that most desktops already have.

## Options

- `--example <n>` open a built-in example (0–8)
- `--view breadboard` start on the breadboard
- `--theme <Light|Dark|Midnight|Blueprint|Sepia|Forest>`
- `--screenshot <file.png>` draw a few frames, save a picture and quit

## Publishing a release

Every push builds the app for all three systems automatically (see the **Actions** tab).
To publish downloads, create a tag that starts with `v` (for example `v1.0.0`) — on GitHub:
**Releases → Draft a new release → Choose a tag → type `v1.0.0` → Publish**. The builds are attached to it a few minutes later.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

content.text: The automatic build already has a Mac entry, but it only makes a bare program file for newer Apple-chip Macs. I'll make it produce a proper double-clickable "Circuit Bench.app" that works on both Apple-chip and Intel Macs. I'll also add a Mac build script and build the app here so you have one right away.

input.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Builds "Circuit Bench.app" for macOS into the dist folder.
# Makes a universal app (Apple chip + Intel) when both Rust targets are installed
# (rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin x86_64-apple-darwin), otherwise one for this Mac.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

APP="dist/Circuit Bench.app"
BIN_NAME="CircuitBench"
VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/.*"(.*)".*/\1/')

has_target() {
  command -v rustup >/dev/null 2>&1 && rustup target list --installed 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$1"
}

rm -rf "$APP"
mkdir -p "$APP/Contents/MacOS" "$APP/Contents/Resources"

if has_target aarch64-apple-darwin && has_target x86_64-apple-darwin; then
  cargo build --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin
  cargo build --release --target x86_64-apple-darwin
  lipo -create -output "$APP/Contents/MacOS/$BIN_NAME" \
    target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/circuit_bench \
    target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/circuit_bench
  echo "Built a universal app (Apple chip + Intel)."
else
  cargo build --release
  cp target/release/circuit_bench "$APP/Contents/MacOS/$BIN_NAME"
  echo "Built an app for this Mac's processor."
fi
chmod +x "$APP/Contents/MacOS/$BIN_NAME"

cat > "$APP/Contents/Info.plist" <<PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>CFBundleName</key><string>Circuit Bench</string>
  <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key><string>Circuit Bench</string>
  <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>io.github.circuitbench</string>
  <key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>$BIN_NAME</string>
  <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
  <key>CFBundleVersion</key><string>$VERSION</string>
  <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key><string>$VERSION</string>
  <key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key><string>10.13</string>
  <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key><true/>
  <key>LSApplicationCategoryType</key><string>public.app-category.education</string>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST

echo "Done: $APP"

# Builds Circuit Bench for Windows, macOS (universal .app) and Linux on every push.
# Pushing a tag such as v1.0.0 also publishes a GitHub Release with the downloads attached.
name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  windows-linux:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            artifact: CircuitBench-windows
            binary: target/release/circuit_bench.exe
            packaged: CircuitBench.exe
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            artifact: CircuitBench-linux
            binary: target/release/circuit_bench
            packaged: CircuitBench
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Linux desktop libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libxkbcommon-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libx11-dev libxcursor-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libwayland-dev

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --release

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --release

      - name: Package
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp "${{ matrix.binary }}" "dist/${{ matrix.packaged }}"
          cp README.md LICENSE dist/
          cd dist
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then
            7z a "../${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip" .
          else
            chmod +x "${{ matrix.packaged }}"
            zip -r "../${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip" .
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
          path: ${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip

      - name: Attach to release
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: ${{ matrix.artifact }}.zip

  macos:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --release

      - name: Build universal app (Apple chip + Intel)
        run: sh build-mac.sh

      - name: Package
        run: |
          cp README.md LICENSE dist/
          cd dist
          ditto -c -k --keepParent "Circuit Bench.app" ../CircuitBench-macos.zip
          zip -j ../CircuitBench-macos.zip README.md LICENSE

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: CircuitBench-macos
          path: CircuitBench-macos.zip

      - name: Attach to release
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: CircuitBench-macos.zip
